audit_findings.title: TYR makes the earnings numerator inconsistent with the current common-equity claim
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (filed TYR consideration $185.200 million, stock consideration $22.642 million, and TYR revenue $47.195 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026)
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation capitalizes pre-TYR owner earnings while using post-TYR shares, cash and financing; omitted TYR earnings understate OE, while omitted acquisition interest and integration costs overstate OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The purchase consideration was comprised of $ 150,000 of cash and $ 24,000 of Cadre common stock, subject to finalization of normal working capital adjustments.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a forecast risk. TYR is large relative to the $49.8 million anchor, but the filing does not separately disclose TYR earnings, so the net direction and amount cannot be determined. The opposing omissions are reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Construct post-close trailing owner earnings including TYR operating results, integration costs, acquisition interest and taxes; reconcile the $62.5 million initial revolver financing with the subsequent $75.0 million term-loan draw; then rerun all scenarios with post-TYR diluted shares and bridge balances.

audit_findings.title: The historical interest burden is not representative of the valuation-date financing cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.100 million pretax annualized gap: $18.580 million annualized from filed first-half 2026 interest expense versus $12.480 million in FY2025; exact post-swap OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level OE model, recurring interest expense reduces the OE numerator rather than debt principal being deducted in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had $308.8 million in outstanding floating rate debt, which bears interest at one-month SOFR (3.72% as of December 31, 2025) plus applicable margin.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated: first-half 2026 interest expense was $9.290 million and debt principal reached $375.956 million. Simple annualization already exceeds FY2025 interest by $6.100 million before reflecting a full period at the June debt level or the July 2026 expiration of $118.125 million of swaps. That recurring difference is large relative to the $49.8 million anchor and is capitalized through every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.action: Calculate the forward annual interest burden using June 2026 principal, facility margins, mandatory amortization and only swaps remaining after July 23, 2026; apply the corresponding tax effect to OE and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: ICOR contingent consideration is a claim ahead of common equity omitted from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.453 million at June 30, 2026, or $0.11 per fully diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: An unpaid acquisition earnout is a senior cash claim that should either reduce the equity bridge or be included once, without an offsetting add-back, in projected OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As part of the ICOR acquisition, the purchase agreement with respect to the acquisition provided for the payment of contingent consideration of up to CDN$ 8,000 (approximately $ 5,797 on the acquisition date) based upon future cumulative net sales during the three-year period ended January 9, 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated, but its current filed fair value equals only about $0.11 per share, versus scenario values of $13.53-$17.49 and a $12.27 gap between the $29.76 market price and the bull value. Deducting it would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that projected OE does not separately include the settlement; if it does not, deduct the June 2026 ICOR liability of $5.453 million from the bridge in the next mechanical rerun.

audit_findings.title: A large foreign-exchange gain may have been capitalized as recurring owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.455 million, equal to 15.0% of the $49.8 million anchor; $2.356 million was identified as unrealized in the 2025 cash-flow reconciliation
audit_findings.mechanism: Any abnormal foreign-exchange gain retained in the OE anchor is projected through the explicit forecast and terminal value as though it were recurring operating earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Other income, net was $7.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to Other expense, net of $4.7 million for the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to changes in foreign currency exchange rates.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the gain was large and volatile, reversing a $4.721 million expense in 2024. It does not demonstrate whether the valuation workpaper removed it. Because the gross item equals 15.0% of anchor OE, inclusion as recurring earnings would be material even though the exact after-tax OE effect is not established.
audit_findings.action: Trace realized and unrealized currency gains and losses through each annual OE calculation, remove or normalize non-operating volatility consistently, and rerun the scenarios if any part of the 2025 gain remains in the anchor.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition costs cannot be treated as nonrecurring if acquisition-led growth supports the forecast
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.149 million of filed 2025 restructuring, transaction and related-party acquisition expense, equal to 18.4% of the $49.8 million anchor; amount removed from OE unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back recurring deal and integration costs raises OE while forecast growth continues to include benefits from an acquisition program that requires those expenditures.
audit_findings.evidence: Acquisitions have been and will continue to be an important component of our growth strategy; however, we will need to integrate these acquired businesses successfully in order for our growth strategy to succeed and for our Company to be profitable.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes both a continuing acquisition strategy and $7.696 million of restructuring and transaction costs plus $1.453 million of related-party expense in 2025. The record does not show whether those expenses were stripped from OE, but their combined scale establishes that the potential treatment is material.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the five-year OE workpaper for add-backs of transaction, restructuring, integration and related-party acquisition expenses; retain those costs or deduct a normalized continuing acquisition-cost allowance from scenarios relying on acquisition-led growth, then rerun.

audit_findings.title: Part of the acquired FY2025 perimeter was outside management's controls assessment
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified (Zircaloy represented 8% of 2025 sales and 12% of the stated asset measure; the subsequent finalized purchase-accounting adjustment was $0.344 million)
audit_findings.mechanism: Errors in contract estimates, working capital, purchase accounting or cut-off could alter historical OE and the reliability of the FY2025 anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Zircaloy’s combined financial statements constitute 12% of total assets (excluding goodwill and intangible assets, which are included within the assessment) and 8% of total sales of the consolidated financial statement amounts as of and for the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The controls exclusion is demonstrated, but it is not evidence that the audited numbers are misstated. Zircaloy's 8% share of sales is too large to dismiss categorically, while the filed $0.344 million subsequent purchase-accounting adjustment does not resolve possible OE-related estimates. The record therefore cannot establish either direction or materiality.
audit_findings.action: Review post-year-end Zircaloy contract-asset and cost-to-complete revisions, working-capital adjustments, finalized purchase accounting, audit adjustments and reported control deficiencies before treating its FY2025 contribution as seasoned recurring OE.
